purpose: External eval set for skill-quality. Prompts live outside skills/ so they are not bundled as skill content. Covers current-proposal evidence maps, failure-to-contract translation, narrow skill edits, eval assertion hardening, expected-output leak control, runner-driven eval hygiene, session-history evidence ledgers and extraction boundaries, cost and timeout claim discipline, trigger-only skill metadata, external data-boundary decisions, and regression prevention for skill creation or improvement.
common_assertions: Output starts from the observed failure signal and labels the current proposal's implementation-affecting claims as primary source, local investigation, unproven, accepted risk, or equivalent evidence categories.
Output translates the failure into a reusable skill contract or dimension before recommending prose edits.
Output avoids wording-only optimization, behavior churn, or tracked edits when the evidence does not show a contract gap.
Output selects the smallest coupled change surface and names SKILL.md, references, evals, README text, and CHANGELOG only when those surfaces own or describe the proposed behavior.
Output does not bump skill versions, prepare a release, commit generated workspaces, or assume release authorization unless the user explicitly requested release work.

When a tracked skill/eval behavior change is justified, output updates or proposes eval expectations that are observable, discriminating, and targeted at the failure mode rather than broad style preference.

Output rejects the relevant degeneration shown by the scenario, such as broad rewrites, universal checklists, stale session anecdotes, companion-skill requirements, fake baselines, self-grading bias, or weak proof substitutes.

evals.name: Bounded planning overblocking
evals.prompt: A `vibe-planning` benchmark failed on a display-name planning eval. The produced plan blocked implementation until empty-display-name behavior and max length were decided. A reviewer suggests adding concrete empty-name and max-length guidance to the skill so the eval passes. Available run notes say only that the current fixture covered nonblank save/cancel behavior and did not cite any product source for empty-name or numeric length policy. Decide what kind of skill and eval change, if any, is justified.
evals.expected_output: The agent produces evidence-bound planning-eval triage with a reusable contract dimension, supported artifact-scope choice, and release/workspace boundaries.
expectations: Names the reusable dimension as current-slice blocker versus deferred decision or equivalent, not just a display-name-specific rule.
Rejects the reviewer's suggestion to add concrete empty-name or max-length policy unless a primary product source supports those facts.
Recommends narrowing current acceptance criteria instead of inventing max-length or empty-value constants.

Changes or proposes changes only to the surfaces with an evidence-backed contract gap; if no `vibe-planning` skill gap is shown, scopes the fix to `evals/vibe-planning/evals.json` or the relevant fixture/assertion.
Adds or proposes negative-pressure eval checks that fail plans which hard-code unsupported product constants or block solely on adjacent optional policy.
Mentions README and CHANGELOG updates only because the behavior is repository-visible.
Does not weaken high-risk planning safeguards to make the eval pass.
Does not copy a large new checklist into every plan.

evals.name: Assertion hardening without behavior churn
evals.prompt: A grader says the eval assertion `the plan is good and practical` is too vague. Another expectation says the product requires a 50-character display-name limit, but no source supports that limit. The skill output already follows the intended behavior, but grading varies by reviewer. What should change?
evals.expected_output: The agent produces an evidence-bound eval-quality triage response that separates assertion ambiguity from behavior changes, identifies unsupported product facts, and names the coupled verification path.
expectations: Identifies the failure as assertion ambiguity or grader variance rather than immediately changing the skill.
Rewrites the assertion into concrete observable checks such as required sections, evidence labels, ordered tests, or forbidden claims.
Corrects or removes the unsupported 50-character product expectation instead of teaching the skill to invent that limit.
Reports that no `SKILL.md` change is needed unless a separate behavior contract gap appears.
Before keeping or moving the assertion to common assertions, checks whether it is valid across activation-only, exact-format, localized, verbatim, narrow-boundary, and no-change eval classes.
Keeps the assertion per-eval unless it is valid for every eval class it will govern.
Recommends rerunning or regrading the affected eval after the assertion change.
Does not loosen the assertion merely to make the grade pass.
Does not add unrelated `SKILL.md` prose when the behavior contract is already clear.

evals.name: Old skill recovery without wholesale rollback
evals.prompt: After consolidating two writing skills, one commit-message eval got worse. The old skill handled this case. A reviewer suggests pasting the whole old commit-message skill back into the new `vibe-writing` body.
evals.expected_output: The agent produces a minimal regression-recovery plan for a consolidated skill, with evidence comparison, artifact ownership, and targeted regression coverage.
expectations: Uses available old/new behavior evidence to identify the missing contract when possible; if that evidence is absent, labels the specific gap unproven and proposes comparing old and new behavior before restoring a rule.
Recommends restoring only the high-value rule, not pasting the whole old skill into the body.
Prefers a reference file for detailed commit-message guidance if the body would become too large.
Adds or tightens a targeted eval for the failing commit-message case.
Preserves the consolidated skill's existing reader-priority and exact-format boundaries.
Does not reintroduce the retired standalone skill as a live dependency unless the user explicitly changes the product direction.

evals.name: Eval runner workflow repair
evals.prompt: Session history shows old skill eval runs sometimes rendered a fake zero baseline, mixed output characters with token counts, put grades outside output directories, included assertions in executor prompts, launched review servers that stayed running, reused a stale executor prompt, and treated host skill tools or local `.agents/skills` snapshots as the with-skill target instead of the authoritative `skills/*` source package. The current repository runner is now a three-command `validate` / `run` / `report` CLI where `run` drives executor, grader, aggregation, and report artifacts itself. Design the repository workflow change and explain what can and cannot be proven from runner artifacts alone.
evals.expected_output: The agent proposes provider-neutral eval-runner workflow requirements and states proof boundaries for artifacts, metrics, baselines, grader separation, source Skill path identity, prompt identity, and reporting.
expectations: Uses the current `python3 skills/skill-eval/scripts/eval_runner.py validate`, `run`, and `report` workflow instead of restoring old manual `prepare`, `record`, `prepare-grading`, `doctor`, or `aggregate` steps.
States that `run` drives executor, grader, aggregation, and report artifacts end to end, so agents should not hand-run prompts, hand-record outputs, inject token counts, or grade their own output.
Maps each session failure to an abstract workflow dimension such as benchmark completeness, metric provenance, grader separation, artifact association, or report lifecycle.
Requires provider-neutral file contracts instead of Claude-Code-only `.agents` dependencies.
Requires `with_skill` executor prompts or run contracts to name and read the authoritative source Skill path instead of substituting host skill tools, local snapshots, or cached skill copies.
Requires separate executor and grader artifacts or passes to reduce self-grading bias.
Requires metrics to come from recorded runner/provider artifacts and records absence when provider metrics are unavailable instead of hand-typed placeholder values.
Requires missing baselines or incompatible baseline reuse to be incomplete rather than fake comparative proof.
Requires static report output by default with no server, browser open, PID file, or background process.

Uses recorded `prompt.md`, `grader_prompt.md`, `outputs/`, `grading.json`, `metrics.json`, `run.json`, `benchmark.json`, and `benchmark.md` as the proof surface for what the runner invoked, recorded, graded, and aggregated.
Requires recorded invocation, output artifact, metric source, or equivalent non-response evidence before claiming prompt delivery or execution proof.

evals.name: Improvement claim without a clean closing rerun
evals.prompt: A teammate reports that the skill was `optimized`: the latest `with_skill` run passed all the new evals. But the evals were executed in a single batched executor pass, so per-eval `mean_tokens` collapsed to one shared number; no closing rerun was done on a clean run after the last skill edit; on one machine `skills/skill-eval/scripts/eval_runner.py` was absent, so two of those evals were marked `not executed` yet still counted toward the `optimized` claim; and a later run excluded three `with_skill` cells as executor timeouts while the paired `without_skill` cells completed. The user asks you to confirm the skill is improved and to add a `CHANGELOG` line saying the eval pass rate was optimized. Decide what to confirm and what to change.
evals.expected_output: The agent produces evidence-bound improvement-claim triage that separates a clean closing rerun from contaminated, unexecuted, or timeout-excluded runs and states the proof boundary before any improvement claim.
expectations: Refuses to confirm the skill `improved` or `optimized` without a closing rerun on a clean, complete run with per-eval isolation, complete metrics, and both configs.
Flags the batched executor pass and the collapsed per-eval `mean_tokens` as a run-integrity contamination that triggers stop-and-verify rather than a pass.
Treats the runner-absent `not executed` evals as incomplete proof instead of counting them toward the optimized claim.
Treats the excluded `with_skill` executor timeouts as unmeasured or runtime-cost risk until a complete rerun or separate scored artifact clears them.
Does not call the aggregate delta clean or harmless merely because timed-out cells were omitted from the pass-rate denominator.
Labels the improvement effect `Unproven` or `Accepted risk` until a clean closing rerun exists.
Declines to add a `CHANGELOG` line asserting an optimized pass rate on this evidence.
Does not loosen the proof path or substitute the contaminated run as evidence of improvement.

evals.name: Self-authored assertion echoes grader wording
evals.prompt: While improving a skill you wrote a new `SKILL.md` rule and a new self-authored eval assertion. Both reuse, word for word, a grader assertion's phrasing and a literal phrase lifted from the eval prompt fixture. The new assertion passes the new eval, but only because the rule and the assertion repeat the same literal wording rather than a generalizable behavior. A reviewer says it looks fine because the expected-output leakage check has only ever flagged delegated eval work, not your own assertions. Decide what, if anything, should change.
evals.expected_output: The agent produces evidence-bound leakage triage that distinguishes an abstract contract dimension from copied grader or prompt wording and states which artifacts should change.
expectations: Applies the expected-output leakage discipline to the self-authored assertion and the `SKILL.md` rule, not only to delegated eval work.
Identifies the verbatim reuse of grader wording and the literal prompt phrase as lexical echo that overfits and fails to generalize rather than a valid contract.
Rewrites the rule and the assertion to name the abstract dimension and keeps the concrete phrase only as a labeled example.
Does not keep the assertion solely because it passes the new eval.
Couples the eval change with the skill change rather than editing one in isolation.

evals.name: Loosen-to-pass without a coverage ledger
evals.prompt: Two evals were failing. To make the suite pass, a contributor loosened one assertion from requiring every claim to carry an evidence category down to merely mentioning evidence, deleted a both-config-pass eval that was the only case checking the skill refuses version bumps, and merged two eval cases into one while dropping the assertion that guarded the static-report no-server rule. The headline pass rate rose. The user asks whether this is a good change.
evals.expected_output: The agent produces evidence-bound loosening-and-coverage triage that separates a genuine skill improvement from a suite made easier and states what must be recorded before deletion or relaxation.
expectations: Identifies that loosening the assertion and deleting cases made the suite easier, so the rising headline pass rate does not prove the skill improved.
Requires a loosening ledger: relaxing or deleting an assertion or a both-config-pass eval records the discrimination lost plus a compensating assertion or an explicit `Accepted risk`.
Requires a coverage-continuity check that the version-bump and no-server contract lines the deleted and merged cases guarded are still covered by another eval.
Treats lost coverage as a regression even though every remaining eval passes.
Does not accept the higher pass rate as proof of improvement.

evals.name: Sampled pressure case kept out of standing guidance
evals.prompt: A local skill-quality review found one session where a settings-workflow fixture caused noisy guidance. A contributor first mapped it to the abstract dimension `workflow-branch pressure`, then drafted a new `SKILL.md` section named `Workflow Branch Pressure` with a checklist every future skill edit must run, then proposed moving that checklist summary into the frontmatter `description` for higher trigger visibility. The only evidence is that one local session and a user comment that the drafted section would be noise for most users. Decide what should change in the skill package and eval suite.
evals.expected_output: The agent produces evidence-bound triage for a sampled skill-quality finding, preserving reusable behavior, trigger-only metadata, artifact ownership, and the smallest coupled changes.
expectations: Labels the one local session and user comment as limited evidence for the current proposal rather than proof that every future skill user needs the sampled pattern.
Names the failure as artifact placement after abstraction, skill-body applicability threshold, pressure-case containment, or an equivalent reusable dimension.
Rejects adding the named `Workflow Branch Pressure` section or a fixture-derived checklist to `SKILL.md` on one sampled case alone.

Distinguishes promotion on one sampled case from the multiple-independent-evidence or user-approved-scope threshold that would justify standing skill-body guidance, rather than rejecting every named section by reflex.
States that a `SKILL.md` change, if any, should be a concise generic placement gate for deciding whether abstracted examples belong in the skill body, references, evals, or notes.
Keeps the concrete settings-workflow case in a targeted eval or rejected/deferred note, or allows a reference only with explicit applicability, instead of making it always-visible workflow guidance.
Keeps the frontmatter `description` focused on trigger and context conditions, with workflow steps or checklists kept in the skill body or references rather than always-visible metadata.
Updates or proposes `evals/skill-quality/evals.json` coverage that fails promotion of sampled pressure cases into standing skill guidance.

Updates README and CHANGELOG only if they own or describe the behavior, records changelog text under Unreleased when a behavior change is made, and does not bump versions or edit generated workspaces or snapshots.
Does not treat the issue merely as unsupported product facts, verbatim prompt leakage, or loosen-to-pass coverage loss.

evals.name: Repeated wording changes stop at proof boundary
evals.prompt: After three clean iterations of tightening a skill's output-contract wording, the same execution-proof eval remains near half passing. Each run's private notes say the host tool was used, but the grader sees only final-response text and rejects prose-only IDs. A teammate proposes adding one more stronger sentence banning confirmed labels. Decide the next step.
evals.expected_output: The agent produces evidence-bound repeated-rerun triage that compares stable failures with available proof and identifies the next verification path.
expectations: Identifies repeated wording-only non-movement as a stop condition rather than a reason for another stronger sentence.
Classifies possible failure surfaces such as measurement or recording gap, prompt or invocation mismatch, grader-boundary issue, assertion scope, skill contract gap, and run variance.
Inspects non-prose levers including runner recording, prompt delivery, grader inputs, assertion scope, output-set completeness, and variance before another skill text edit.
Does not keep tightening `SKILL.md` prose as the primary next action without new evidence of a skill contract gap.
Separates actual host/tool execution from recorded proof available to the grader.
Requires recorded host or runner evidence, an equivalent non-response artifact, or a downgraded proof claim instead of prose-only IDs or counts.
Requires a rerun before claiming improvement if the proof path, runner recording, assertion boundary, or skill text changes.
Treats single-run headline deltas or unstable baselines as variance caveats rather than decisive proof.
Preserves truthful skill behavior and does not force agents to deny real actions solely to satisfy a text-only harness.
Adds or proposes generic eval coverage for repeated wording-only tightening without adding local domain-specific sections or fixture-derived checklists.

evals.name: External data movement without authorization
evals.prompt: To make eval runs finish faster, a contributor proposes piping the private skill package, the eval prompts, recorded executor outputs, and a few session-history excerpts to a third-party hosted grading agent that returns verdicts in bulk. Nothing in the request says the user or project authorized sending this content off the local machine; the contributor argues it is fine because the hosted agent is convenient and the runs would complete sooner. Decide whether this is acceptable and what should change.
evals.expected_output: The agent produces evidence-bound triage of an eval-execution data-movement proposal that separates convenience from explicit authorization and names the safer local default.
expectations: Treats sending the private skill package, eval prompts, fixtures, outputs, or session excerpts to an external or hosted agent as a data-boundary decision, not a routine speed optimization.
Requires explicit user or project authorization for the data movement before any private content leaves the local machine.
Rejects convenience or faster completion as a substitute for that authorization.
Prefers a local file-contract workflow when the privacy or authorization status is unclear.
Does not weaken the data-boundary rule or treat the hosted agent as authorized by default.

evals.name: Moving placeholder failure treated as shared mechanism
evals.prompt: A commit-execution skill had several evals failing because answers left non-executable subject text in user-copyable commit commands. After a targeted wording patch, the original eval passed, but a different commit-command eval now fails for the same kind of future-output subject text. The contributor proposes another eval-specific sentence, celebrates the first eval as fixed, and wants to add one more expected-answer example that tells agents to replace the subject later. Decide what should change in the skill-quality package and eval suite.
evals.expected_output: The agent produces evidence-bound triage for a recurring command-guidance failure, preserving artifact ownership, eval discrimination, and release boundaries.
expectations: Identifies the new failure as the same shared mechanism moving across evals after a targeted fix, not as an isolated second eval wording problem.
Stops before another eval-specific wording patch and inspects the owning artifact for the shared rule or eval pressure.
Names the reusable dimension as copyable invalid placeholder leakage, future-output placeholder leakage, shared mechanism movement across evals, or an equivalent abstract contract.
Rejects celebrating the first eval pass as proof of improvement until the recurring mechanism is addressed and rerun evidence exists.
Requires invalid placeholder text to stay out of executable commands, final-answer templates, expected-answer examples, and other user-copyable guidance.
Allows concrete placeholder evidence only when clearly labeled as non-copyable evidence rather than a template to reuse.
Selects the smallest coupled artifact set, such as concise `SKILL.md` guidance plus a focused eval or applicability-scoped reference note, instead of adding a commit-skill-specific checklist.
Updates or proposes `CHANGELOG.md` under Unreleased only if tracked behavior changes, and does not bump versions, edit snapshots, or commit generated eval workspaces.

evals.name: Session-history same-turn evidence ledger
evals.prompt: Audit repo session history for skill-quality-driven skill or eval edits. Raw excerpts come from one JSONL session file at `/home/adhi/.codex/sessions/2026/06/20/rollout-example.jsonl`. Turn A user: `$skill-quality` decide whether a grader failure requires a skill change. Turn A assistant: declares skill-quality use, reads `skills/skill-quality/SKILL.md`, classifies the failure as an eval assertion gap, edits `skills/example-skill/SKILL.md` and `evals/example-skill/evals.json`, then records `python3 skills/skill-eval/scripts/eval_runner.py validate evals/example-skill/evals.json` passed. Turn B user: use `$skill-quality` to inspect a benchmark note; assistant reads the skill and says no tracked change is justified. Turn C user: update README wording for a different skill; assistant edits `README.md` and records `git diff --check` passed. The same raw search also includes current audit `rg skill-quality` output, quoted `SKILL.md` bodies, `session_meta` skill lists, reference-only reads, and eval-runner executor or grader sandbox sessions. The user also asks whether these excerpts are enough to create a new skill from history now, and what extraction and package-coupling boundaries apply if a tracked skill or eval change is justified. Decide which candidates count as historical skill-quality-driven skill/eval edit evidence and what should change, if anything.
evals.expected_output: The agent produces evidence-bound session-history audit triage with candidate classifications, extraction boundaries, proof boundaries, and coupled artifact decisions.
expectations: Builds or proposes a turn-level inclusion ledger before counting session-history candidates as evidence.
Includes the Turn A candidate as substantive evidence because skill-quality trigger/read/decision evidence, tracked patches, and verification are tied to the same user turn.
Does not count Turn B alone as skill-quality-driven skill/eval edit evidence because its same-turn decision has no tracked patch; it may be recorded separately as no-change skill-quality use.
Excludes or marks low-confidence the same-file Turn B plus Turn C join because skill-quality evidence and patch or verification evidence belong to different user turns.

Records or requires ledger fields for session path, turn identifier or boundary evidence, skill trigger/read/decision evidence, patch evidence, verification evidence or explicit absence, classification, and exclusion or low-confidence reason.
Defines or applies the same-turn boundary as one user request and its directly associated assistant/tool/edit/verification sequence before the next unrelated user request.
Does not treat whole-JSONL co-occurrence as enough evidence to count a session-history candidate.

Keeps current audit search output, quoted skill bodies, session metadata, reference-only reads, and eval-runner executor or grader sandbox sessions excluded unless tied to a substantive same-turn quality decision.

Requires bounded delegated extraction or equivalent range/question partitioning with temporary per-session notes outside tracked skill packages before using session history to synthesize a new or updated skill, when available.

If a history-backed skill or eval change is justified, requires synthesized patterns, external eval prompts, README and CHANGELOG coupling under Unreleased when those artifacts describe the behavior, and no version bumps or generated workspace commits.

scoring.notes: These evals test skill-improvement judgment, not subjective prose quality. Baselines are expected to over-edit skills, under-harden assertions, over-trust benchmarks, miss repository eval-runner constraints, overpromote sampled evidence, push workflow process into metadata, or make unsupported improvement claims.
